recorded_boundaries.text: These are the premises of the universally quantified target, not independently supplied existence results.
This is the setting of the manuscript theorem; it is not a finite-instance algorithmic runtime guarantee.
The diffusion premise belongs to the first two conjuncts of value_consequences. Its final ground-state/Parisi equality has only the minimizer premise.
This records the minimizer premise of the formal interface; it does not assert that a minimizer exists.
The extensive uncut Hamiltonian need not have an operator limit. Smallness of a generator on a core alone is not the needed exponential or domain statement.

The proof first fixes outer Lipschitz constants, then inner errors, using seed truncation, the regularized inverse sine, cutoffs and Fourier approximation. Approximation is in the rooted L² norm, not merely in marginal distribution.
This query root keeps the fixed-minimizer hypothesis in scope and exposes the complete conditional scalar-to-rooted construction. It is not a declaration that a minimizer exists.

Closed witness application: attainment supplies gamma in the manuscript class U, and the universally quantified fixed-minimizer construction uses that same gamma before any finite choices are frozen. Its annotated support edge exposes the conditional argument while discharging the supplied manuscript admissibility and minimizer premises only within this use. The binding is authored source correspondence, not mechanically checked witness equality or proof acceptance.
Disjoint mask orthogonality and the Gaussian isometry control the loss. Shared descendant branches are not assumed independent. Uniform derivative bounds refer to the original grouped coordinates.
Both norm convergence and the occupation bound are hypotheses. Strong convergence or one-point distributional convergence by itself does not permit multiplying an edge correlation by √D.
Equality of seed marginals or ordinary Gram convergence does not alone prove rooted energy convergence. The displayed L-pairing calculation is a separate ingredient.
BFMVZ Theorem 1 is a fixed-depth, fixed-angle identity. It does not transfer raw seeded, masked or controlled words, give a joint n,p,D limit, or certify the construction preceding seed removal.

Measurable seed masks are permitted through bounded subsequences with Gaussian almost-everywhere convergence. Grouped finite control coordinates are essential; no dimension-free assertion is made for all flattened color coordinates.

The receiving root seed is independent of these child fields. The first-chaos identity is an identity in the shared rooted space; a marginal Gaussian law alone does not identify E(v). This is a manuscript construction, not a Lean declaration.

First fix the finite input channels and surrounding word. Helper pinning concerns all helper descendants, not only the receiver root. Individual approximating commutator factors need not preserve that subspace. Lower first responses and scalar second responses must be retained; covariance between channels cannot be discarded.

This is finite approximation of selected local rooted operations. It is not a uniform global operator-norm Trotter estimate on an extensive Hamiltonian, and no error may be multiplied by a growing vertex count.

The finite word and all angles are held fixed before D→∞. Rotated axes and a seed gate exp(−it Zs) have the corresponding rooted formulas; this calculation alone is not a transfer theorem for seeded words.

This is an existence statement for one common finite word. Cost gates, mixers, identity padding and combining adjacent equal gate types convert it to the standard alternating QAOA convention. The tree-to-SK step is still a separate theorem.
The exponential statement has its own domain and weighted Gronwall argument. It is not inferred solely from a small Hilbert–Schmidt kernel or small generator.

This realizes both the finite scalar joint law and its shifted energy pairing. It does not assert strong finite-degree convergence for the unsmoothed sign formula. Intermediate transmitted columns need not be bounded.
The full displaced packets may have occupation of order r^(−2); only their tails have uniform weighted bounds. No uniform whole-packet occupation bound is imported from the finite-word degree limit.

Some ordinary angles are of order 1/r and can be very large, but are finite before any degree or system-size limit. The theorem gives no bound on word length, angle size or an efficient search procedure.

The same vertex seed is reused in every seed gate. Compilation proceeds outer rank to inner rank: pointwise approximants, sender partitions, finite commutators, then lower ranks; raw-seed masks are compiled last. No uniformity as helper probabilities vanish or circuit length grows is claimed.
One must prove the net o(r) cancellation. Replacing a moving insertion by an O(r)-accurate approximation and subsequently multiplying that error by 1/r is not valid.
The word is finite after the projection list is fixed. This is exact finite-list ensemble control of limiting packet data, not a uniform control statement over a continuum of unknown centers.
The order is terminal cutoff, finite scalar mesh, then finite smoothing. The statement has no joint-limit or uniform-in-terminal-time rate and still allows unbounded intermediate columns.

The displacement limit uses the o(r) error and the actual insertion change. Norm remainders are transported through unitaries; an unbounded observable is not applied to an uncontrolled norm remainder.
No maximizer of the noncompact angle supremum is required; no exact optimality at finite depth is inferred.

The construction must not choose a list from its own as-yet-unproved small-r limit. The perturbation preserves the target energy by continuity; it supplies finite nonvanishing conditions, not a uniform numerical lower bound over all words.

Uniformity concerns a fixed finite calculation, bounded parameter sets and specified weighted norms. It does not imply global operator-norm convergence, a nondegenerate covariance assumption, or uniformity in growing word length.

Pure zero-field SK with covariance normalization xi(t)=t^2/2. Conditional on the supplied order parameter being an admissible integrable minimizer; no separate assertion that a minimizer exists. FullSupportConclusion includes Stieltjes-measure and diffusion existence, full relative support, strict increase, and the two selected diffusion moment identities. It does not assert QAOA circuit-energy convergence.

passages.text:
The full-support manuscript proves that an admissible integrable minimizer
of the zero-temperature Parisi functional for the pure zero-field
Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model has Stieltjes support equal to every overlap
scale in [0,1). The proof turns a hypothetical support gap into a constant
interval for the order parameter. Variational contact at the ends of that
interval conflicts with a strict curvature inequality inside it. Along the
auxiliary diffusion, the spatial gradient of the value function is a bounded
martingale. Full support makes this martingale's second moment equal to time;
its terminal correlation with Brownian motion gives the ground-state value.
The manuscript's further argument gives a smooth Stieltjes density, strictly
positive on $(0,1)$, and no atom at zero. Sections 9.1–9.2 derive this stronger
ordinary conclusion separately from the selected formal support statement.

This record reconstructs those arguments and follows the finite Gaussian
approximation into the separate QAOA manuscript. The latter claims that
finite deterministic circuits approach the SK optimum when system size tends
to infinity before circuit depth increases. Its circuit construction needs
additional approximation, synthesis, seed-removal and transfer arguments.
The two formal statements concern full support and scalar value
consequences; neither states QAOA circuit convergence. Their verification
scope is described at the end. See [OpenAI (2026a), §§1–2][fs-main] and
[OpenAI (2026b), Theorem 1.1][q-intro].

Write $u=\Phi_x$, $a=\Phi_{xx}$, and
$dX_t=\gamma(t)u(t,X_t)\,dt+dB_t$, $X_0=0$.
Write $q(t)=\mathbb E[u(t,X_t)^2]$ for the second moment of this
gradient along $X$.
The first result assumes an admissible minimizer. It constructs its
Stieltjes measure and an associated diffusion, proves
$\operatorname{supp}\mu_\gamma=[0,1)$ and strict increase of $\gamma$,
and obtains $\mathbb E u(t,X_t)^2=t$ and
$\mathbb E a(t,X_t)^2=1$ for every associated diffusion. The selected
formal statement has exactly this conditional scope; it does not assert a
smooth density.
Its [Lean implementation at the fixed source revision][support-main] implements the
[separately stated formal challenge][support-type]. The
[Comparator configuration][support-config] identifies the intended
comparison; the evidence retained with this draft does not establish
a successful research-target replay.

The second result concerns the scalar value. A bounded martingale ends
at a spin-valued random variable whose Brownian correlation represents
$P_*$. Finite Gaussian coefficients approximate that correlation at each
fixed $T<1$, followed by $T\uparrow1$. Its formal statement is separate
and retains the minimizer and diffusion hypotheses where needed. The QAOA
theorem goes further: for each requested accuracy it selects one finite
deterministic circuit, independent of size and disorder, whose limiting
expected energy approaches $P_*$. Neither formal statement asserts that
circuit conclusion.
The scalar clauses are in a [separate Lean implementation][value-main], with their
own [formal challenge][value-type] and [Comparator configuration][value-config].
Those links identify the selected statements, not a completed replay
receipt for either research target.

passages.text: **Theorem 5.1 (full support).** In the pure zero-field SK model with $\xi(t)=t^2/2$, let $\gamma\in\mathcal U$ minimize $\mathcal P$. Then $\operatorname{supp}\mu_\gamma=[0,1)$ and $\gamma$ is strictly increasing. For every associated diffusion started at zero, $\mathbb E u(t,X_t)^2=t$ and $\mathbb E a(t,X_t)^2=1$ for $0\le t<1$. Keep the same minimiser, diffusion and moment function $q$ throughout. Section 3 has established $G\ge0$, $G=0$ on the support $S=\operatorname{supp}\mu_\gamma$, and the contact conditions $q(s)=s$, $q'(s)\le1$ at support points. At zero, the value identity comes from symmetry, and the slope bound requires $0\in S$. Section 4 supplies curvature on constant intervals for every admissible coefficient. These premises are available before any support gap is excluded. We first deal with the endpoint at one, then use the curvature estimate on the remaining intervals. For a terminal interval $(a,1)$, including empty support $[0,1)$, the cusp estimate gives $1-q(t)\gtrsim\sqrt{1-t}$ and hence $G<0$ near one. On a positive plateau with two contact endpoints, strict convexity puts $q'$ below its endpoint chord, although its integral must equal the interval length. On a zero plateau the heat argument makes $q'$ strictly increasing, below the right contact slope. At an initial gap, use the one-sided contact slope if $0\in S$; otherwise the coefficient is zero and symmetry supplies $q(0)=0$. **Why a terminal plateau violates the variational inequality.** Suppose that $\gamma=c$ on $(a,1)$, where $0\le a<1$ and $c\ge0$ is finite. The endpoint $1$ is outside the support domain, so there is no contact condition there to complete an endpoint-chord argument. Instead we will prove $$ 1-q(t)\ge C\sqrt{1-t} \tag{5.1} $$ for some $C>0$ and every $t$ sufficiently close to one. The proof separates two facts: the diffusion puts positive probability density near zero, and the smoothed terminal slope has a definite deficit from $\pm1$ in a shrinking window around zero. Fix $s\in(a,1)$ and let $\rho_s$ be the law of $X_s$. Choose $R<\infty$ such that $p_0=\rho_s([-R,R])>0$. For $c>0$, set $$ h(t,y)=\mathbb E e^{c|y+\sqrt{1-t}Z|},\qquad \Phi(t,y)=c^{-1}\log h(t,y), $$ where $Z$ is standard normal. The drift on this interval is $c\Phi_x=h_x/h$, and the transition density is $$ k_{s,t}(x,y)=p_{t-s}(y-x)\frac{h(t,y)}{h(s,x)},\qquad p_v(z)=(2\pi v)^{-1/2}e^{-z^2/(2v)}. \tag{5.2} $$ The heat-semigroup identity normalises this kernel; equivalently, for Brownian motion started at $(s,x)$, $h(t,B_t)/h(s,x)$ is the positive mean-one change of measure which adds the drift $h_x/h$. For $c=0$, the same kernel formula applies with $h=1$, and the value function is the ordinary heat evolution of $|x|$. [OpenAI (2026a), Lemma 6.3, proof of (6.6)][fs-var]. Put $L=1-s$ and $\delta=L/2$. For $s+\delta\le t<1$, $|x|\le R$ and $|y|\le1$, $$ p_{t-s}(y-x)\ge (2\pi L)^{-1/2}e^{-(R+1)^2/(2\delta)}=:k_*>0, $$ while $h(t,y)\ge1$ and $h(s,x)\le e^{cR}\mathbb E e^{c\sqrt L|Z|}=:M<\infty$. Integrating (5.2) over the part of $\rho_s$ in $[-R,R]$ therefore gives a density $f_t$ of $X_t$ with $$ f_t(y)\ge p_0k_*/M=:m>0 \quad(s+\delta\le t<1,\ |y|\le1). \tag{5.3} $$ Only positive mass of a compact set was needed at time $s$; no density assumption on $\rho_s$ has entered. Now write $\varepsilon=1-t$ and restrict to $|y|\le\sqrt\varepsilon$. Differentiating the terminal heat formula gives, with the unweighted interpretation for $c=0$, $$ u(t,y)= \frac{\mathbb E[\operatorname{sgn}(y+\sqrt\varepsilon Z) e^{c|y+\sqrt\varepsilon Z|}]} {\mathbb E e^{c|y+\sqrt\varepsilon Z|}}. $$ The denominator is at most $D=e^c\mathbb E e^{c|Z|}<\infty$. Each sign has unnormalised mass at least $p_*:=\mathbb P(Z\ge1)>0$: the threshold $|y/\sqrt\varepsilon|$ is at most one, and the exponential weight is at least one. Hence each sign has tilted probability at least $\theta=p_*/D\in(0,1/2)$. It follows that $$ |u(t,y)|\le1-2\theta,\qquad 1-u(t,y)^2\ge4\theta(1-\theta)=:\kappa>0. $$ Multiplying this uniform deficit by the density lower bound (5.3) and the window width $2\sqrt\varepsilon$ yields $$ 1-q(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}(1-u(t,y)^2)f_t(y)\,dy \ge 2m\kappa\sqrt{1-t}. $$ This proves (5.1) with $C=2m\kappa$. [OpenAI (2026a), Lemma 6.3, density and terminal-window estimates][fs-var]. The sign of the contradiction is now explicit. For $s'$ sufficiently close to one, the estimate holds at every $t\in[s',1)$, so $$ \begin{aligned} G(s')&=\int_{s'}^1(q(t)-t)\,dt\\ &\le\frac{(1-s')^2}{2} -\frac{2C}{3}(1-s')^{3/2}<0. \end{aligned} $$ The final inequality holds once $\sqrt{1-s'}<4C/3$. It contradicts the nonnegative cost of adding an atom at $s'$. This proof covers $c=0$ as well as $c>0$. In particular, empty support is impossible: then $\mu_\gamma=0$ and $\gamma=0$ on all of $[0,1)$. The terminal-plateau conclusion was already recorded in [Auffinger, Chen and Zeng (2020), Remark 7][acz]; the estimates above supply the quantitative argument needed here. The terminal gap is now excluded. The support proof resumes with [the remaining finite components](#finite-gap-cases); the next argument gives a shorter route to the same exclusion, without its quantitative bound. **A shorter qualitative exclusion.** The existing curvature input also excludes a terminal support gap without estimating its boundary layer. The [zero-interval argument](#zero-plateau) makes $q$ strictly convex on $[0,1)$, whereas the positive-plateau argument above makes $q'$ strictly convex. Here $q(0)=0$ and $0\le q\le1$. Its complement is a union of relative open intervals, and the Stieltjes measure vanishes on each such interval. For $x First consider a gap $(a,b)$ with both endpoints in $S$, allowing $a=0$. Compact-strip regularity gives continuity of $q'$ on $[a,b]$, even if $\gamma$ jumps at an endpoint. Contact gives $$ q(a)=a,\qquad q(b)=b,\qquad q'(a),q'(b)\le1. \tag{5.4} $$ If the constant coefficient is $c>0$, Section 4 makes $q'$ strictly convex in the gap. Continuity extends the chord comparison to its endpoints, giving $$ q'(t)<\frac{b-t}{b-a}q'(a)+\frac{t-a}{b-a}q'(b)\le1, \qquad a With $h=q'$ and $C_{a,b}$ its endpoint chord, the contradiction is the exact area identity $$ (b-a)-\int_a^b h =(b-a)\left(1-\frac{h(a)+h(b)}2\right) +\int_a^b(C_{a,b}-h)>0. $$ The first term is nonnegative; strict convexity makes the second positive. Only continuity of $q'$ is needed at the ends. For example, a jump $\Delta\gamma$ at $s$ gives the one-sided identity $$ q''(s+)-q''(s-)=-2\Delta\gamma\,\mathbb E a(s,X_s)^3. $$ It follows by applying Itô's formula to $a^2$ and using continuity of its derivative moments on a compact strip. Taking $\gamma=0$ before $s=1/2$ and $\gamma=1/2$ afterward makes this jump strictly negative; the terminal Cole–Hopf solution has positive Hessian. Thus continuity of $q'$ does not license classical higher time derivatives across coefficient jumps. [OpenAI (2026a), proof of Corollary 6.4][fs-density]. If $(0,b)$ is a gap and $0\in S$, the preceding proof applies using the one-sided contact slope bound at zero. Because $(0,b)$ contains no mass, the support condition at zero forces an atom there and hence $c=\gamma(0)>0$. Its absence has not been proved at this stage. If instead the complementary component is $[0,b)$ with $0\notin S$, there is no mass anywhere in $[0,b)$. Thus $\gamma=0$ there. The identity $q(0)=0$ comes from zero-field symmetry, and the right endpoint gives $q(b)=b$, $q'(b)\le1$. Here $q''(t)>0$ for $0 Finally, every nonempty open subinterval $(a,b)$ receives positive mass. Therefore $$ \gamma(b)-\gamma(a)=\mu_\gamma((a,b])>0 \qquad(0\le a0$ is already impossible: either $h\le1$ everywhere, forcing $h\equiv1$ by its integral, or it attains an interior maximum above one, where $h'=0$ and $h''\le0$. This is an elementary deduction from these premises. Chen's conditional crossing theorem, with its own hypotheses, is of this form; §4 proves the stronger $q'''>0$ throughout a positive plateau, without a minimizer premise. See [Chen, arXiv:2607.18032v1, Proposition 4.2 and the proof of Proposition 4.3][chen26]. Neither statement supplies terminal contact at the excluded endpoint one.

passages.text:
### 12.1 The support statement and the derivative bridge

The first formal statement assumes a Brownian system and an admissible
minimizer. It supplies a Stieltjes measure, an associated diffusion, full
relative support and strict increase, and the two moment identities for
every associated diffusion. Its proof assembles contact, exclusion of a
terminal plateau, curvature for positive and zero constant intervals,
and uniqueness to transfer the moments between associated diffusions.
This describes the inspected proof's mathematical route; no successful
research-target replay is claimed. Its quantifiers are
$\forall W\,\forall\gamma$, followed by the minimizer hypothesis;
it supplies both witnesses on the given Brownian system. The moment
conclusion is universal over every diffusion satisfying the specified
equation, and covers exactly $0\le t<1$. The diffusion equation itself
holds through time one, simultaneously for all those times outside
one null set. Controls are progressive for the natural filtration of
Brownian increments and bounded by one pointwise. These are not
additional regularity or minimizer-existence assumptions. See the
[exact support statement][support-type] and the companion
[source-interface review](https://github.com/wcook04/lean-exposition/blob/21b1f9e995c4276fdad02377b378f11541a3d5e9/papers/qaoa-sk/source-review/full-support-interface.md).

There is one useful distinction between the manuscript's first variation
and its formal counterpart. The formal result initially gives a derivative
along chord lengths $1/(n+1)$. For this particular control functional,
that sampled limit determines the ordinary feasible right derivative.
With a control fixed, the terminal absolute value is convex in the
coefficient while the penalty is linear. The supremum over the same
control class, and then subtraction of the linear Parisi penalty,
preserve convexity. The secant slopes therefore vary monotonically as
the chord shortens; each intervening chord lies between two successive
sampled chords and has the same limiting slope. If $\eta$ is an
integrable feasible direction, choose $\varepsilon_0>0$ so that
$\gamma+\varepsilon_0\eta$ is admissible and rescale the chord. This
bridge is an ordinary deduction from the definitions and sampled limit,
not an additional formally named theorem.

At the origin, the manuscript smoothly extends auxiliary quotient
variables. The formal coercivity proof for the spatial diffusion density instead works on the positive
half-line, controls the zero flux at the origin and reflects. What must
agree is the resulting integrated inequality; auxiliary values at zero
need not coincide. In particular, the declared generic flux lemma has
a global derivative hypothesis that is not the supplier used here:
the finite-density proof uses the Gaussian half-line coercivity lemma
and reflection. A totalized quotient value at zero cannot silently
satisfy the generic global hypothesis. The precise source spans are in
the correspondence record.
The [fixed-time supplier `actual_coercivity`][support-fixed-time] assumes
positive time and continuity of the coefficient at that time. Its scaled
polynomial inequality is (4.1) multiplied by $c^2$; division requires
$c>0$. This gives a direct source destination for Proposition 4.1 without
adding a minimizing or plateau premise.
passages.rationale: Support interface and ordinary convexity bridge from sampled chord slopes; preserves half-line coercivity rather than applying an inapplicable generic flux lemma.

passages.text:
The full-support theorem and scalar-value theorem use related but
different formal representations. Their mathematical conclusions can be
discussed together, but a direct formal implication would require the
coefficient, Brownian law, control value and diffusion translations
described in §12, with common witnesses. The finite Gaussian result
also needs its rooted energy identification before it says anything
about a QAOA circuit. The boundedness, regularization, synthesis and
transfer estimates in §8 are additional steps, with temperature-specific
hypotheses where the positive-temperature route is used.

Infinite support allows gaps. An indefinite curvature identity does not imply
strict convexity before expectation is controlled. An algebraic certificate
does not establish its analytic hypotheses. Coordinatewise convergence does
not control a growing coefficient sum. A finite-dimensional Gaussian law
does not identify an energy observable without its operator argument.
Separate witnesses cannot be merged silently. The order
$\forall\varepsilon\ \exists\text{finite word}\ \lim_{n\to\infty}$
cannot be replaced by a fixed-instance depth limit.

The local comparison in §11.1 concerns two printed finite-step displays;
it neither replaces the cited theorem's hypotheses nor supplies the
remaining circuit estimates.

The source collection retains the two manuscripts, formal statements,
their implementations and build metadata. The derived project specifies
Lean 4.34.1 and a pinned mathlib revision. The proof-assistant and library
infrastructure is described by [de Moura and Ullrich (2021), *The Lean 4
Theorem Prover and Programming Language*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-79876-5_37)
and [The mathlib Community (2020), *The Lean Mathematical Library*](https://doi.org/10.1145/3372885.3373824).
These references credit the software; the retained project metadata identifies
the versions used for this source. The retained polynomial computation
in §4 uses exact rational arithmetic. Its expansion matches
all 22 positive remainder
coefficients. The surplus of the $v^4$ coefficient above $1/1000$ is
$140507/1521000000$. This finite check does not establish the PDE
signs, integrability, boundary flux or limiting argument.

The source-byte audit verified the inspected edition; it did not prove
its claims. Paper assembly checked identifiers, declared scope and
document bindings, not semantic correspondence or reader understanding.
Tool-compatibility checks and synthetic fixtures exercised their stated
cases, not either selected SK theorem. Reading of the mathematical and
formal sources supports the bounded comparisons reported here, without
a complete independent proof acceptance or transitive axiom audit.

The retained observations must be kept separate. The original graph records
unrun plans and an earlier full-support attempt that could not start
because the Comparator executable was unavailable. A later retained
attempt, observed on 23 October 2026, built and exported the challenge,
then stopped while building the implementing solution. The retained
[partial-observation receipt](https://github.com/wcook04/lean-exposition/blob/21b1f9e995c4276fdad02377b378f11541a3d5e9/examples/qaoa-sk/verification/full-support-build-failure-20261023.json)
and [log](https://github.com/wcook04/lean-exposition/blob/21b1f9e995c4276fdad02377b378f11541a3d5e9/examples/qaoa-sk/verification/full-support-build-failure-20261023.log) preserve that event: the imported
object for `Diffusion/AbsIncrement` was missing. The challenge is an
admitted specification, so its successful build and export are not a
proof of the theorem. There was no successful solution export or
research-target comparison in that observation.

The scalar-value invocation in the same original two-target run reached
a terminal failure observed on 24 October 2026. Its challenge built and
exported, but its solution build stopped because the imported object for
`Gaussian/IntegralPositiveMulGaussian` was missing. The retained scalar
receipt and log establish no solution export, kernel acceptance or
comparison acceptance. The companion source review locates both records.
Both failures concern the original build configuration. A subsequent
repair to the derived configuration was recorded. In the subsequent
corrected replay, the full-support challenge built and its exporter was
observed running. Reconciliation on 25 October found that the controller
had stopped without a recovered terminal research result. At that date,
Comparator and research extraction outcomes were unknown, neither
rejected nor accepted. The [interruption receipt](https://github.com/wcook04/lean-exposition/blob/21b1f9e995c4276fdad02377b378f11541a3d5e9/examples/qaoa-sk/verification/corrected-replay-interruption-20261025.json)
retains this observation separately from the original build failures.

A subsequent [source-bound observation of 26 October 2026](https://wcook04.github.io/lean-exposition-site/verification/full-support-build-extraction-observation-20261026.json)
records a successful local Lake build of the Support implementation and
v2 extraction of the single conditional full-support root. Its selected
traversal contains 1,674 declarations. The root reports no sorry, unsafe
or partial flag, and its recorded transitive axiom names are
`propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The selected in-scope
traversal completed, but dependencies outside it remain unresolved
boundaries; the extracted graph is partial. This does not establish
minimiser existence, positive density, the scalar target or QAOA convergence.

The portable observation identifies the original receipts by their hashes
and retains the source inventory, root and extraction limits. Its
internal-consistency checks are not authenticated execution provenance.
The curated paper graph records the build and documentary extraction
observation separately; it is not the extracted declaration graph.
Comparator acceptance, standalone kernel replay and the scalar-target
results remain pending. The earlier failed and interrupted invocations
remain dated history, rather than evidence of a later rejection or
acceptance. Permitted axioms and checker settings describe the requested
comparison; they cannot supply its missing result.

This editorial revision does not establish a new formal result.
The [source review through 26 October 2026](https://github.com/wcook04/lean-exposition/blob/ef46d0e72787c1dc283733b10b433d112f97ac64/papers/qaoa-sk/source-review/references-and-adversarial-review.md)
records the preceding paper revision's reading coverage, finite checks,
unsuccessful observations and remaining obligations; viewing it requires
repository access. This remains a draft after source-based agent review;
independent mathematical acceptance and a human reconstruction study
have not been performed.
